papers.title: Single-cell analysis identifies concurrent type 2 and interferon programs in experimental eosinophilic esophagitis
papers.abstract: Background & Aims: Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) is a chronic, type 2 cytokine-driven allergic disease of the esophagus. How the immune and structural cell landscape of the esophagus changes between healthy and inflamed tissue requires further investigation. Methods: CD45-enriched esophageal cells from naive and oxazolone (OXA)-challenged wild-type mice were profiled by single-cell RNA sequencing. A cytokine-gated gene expression score identified type 2 program-high cells. Findings were compared with published human esophageal datasets, validated histologically, and examined in Il13ra1-/- mice. Results: A total of 62,245 esophageal cells were analyzed. ILC2s accounted for most type 2 cytokine-expressing lymphocytes in naive mice, whereas Th2 cells accounted for approximately 80% following OXA challenge. ILC2s concurrently lost Il5, Il13 and Gata3 expression while retaining Areg. Resident memory-like CD8 T cells became the largest lymphoid population. Mast cells switched from a connective tissue-type to a mucosal-type and partly cycling state, which was confirmed by increased MCPT1 cells. Esophageal eosinophils displayed a signature resembling skin eosinophils of atopic dermatitis rather than gastrointestinal eosinophils. Il13ra1-/- mice were protected from epithelial proliferation, thickening and eosinophilia. An interferon-associated program characterized lymphoid, myeloid and structural compartments, and its epithelial component was conserved in human EoE. Conclusions: Th2 cells and mucosal-type mast cells are the dominant sources of type 2 cytokines in experimental EoE. This study further identifies a conserved interferon-associated program that accompanies the type 2 response in the immune and structural compartments of the esophagus and highlights it as a candidate contributor to EoE pathology.

papers.title: IPF Patient Derived Lung Macrophages are Crucial In Signaling Fibroblast Activation and Disease Pathogenesis
papers.abstract: The role of lung macrophage-generated paracrine signals such as TGFb in activating fibroblasts in the pathogenesis of Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) in humans remains uncertain. Here, employing lung macrophages derived from Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) patients and genomic, proteomic and cell function analysis of macrophages, we showed increased generation of TGFb over a period of 48 hours indicative of aberrantly activated macrophages. In cell culture studies, we demonstrated that macrophages markedly activated lung fibroblasts. By inducing actin reorganization in fibroblasts coupled to increased membrane tension, cell contractility, and expression of alpha-smooth muscle actin (SMA) and fibroblast activation protein (FAP). Genomic analysis further revealed augmented collagen synthesis, extracellular matrix (ECM) crosslinking, and activation of pro-survival pathways. IPF macrophages exhibited a threefold increase in surface expression of the mannose receptor CD206, which we exploited using mannose-decorated nanoparticles to selectively deliver TGFb siRNA. The nanoparticle mediated TGFb siRNA delivery prevented these manifestations of fibroblast activation. Genomic analysis showed that TGFb promoted FOXO-mediated expression of COL1A1 in fibroblasts coupled to decreased expression of Matrix Metalloproteinases MMP2 and MMP11. Together, these findings establish macrophage-derived TGFb as a key driver of fibroblast activation in human IPF and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of macrophage-targeted nanoparticle-mediated gene silencing.

papers.title: Filtration attenuates cannabis smoke-induced impacts on primary human airway epithelial cells
papers.abstract: Rationale: Combustion of cannabis flower and inhalation into the lungs exposes the airway epithelium to toxic particulates and gases. Whether cigarette-style cellulose-acetate filtration, a standard for tobacco cigarettes, attenuates epithelial injury and how it affects cannabinoid capture remain unclear. Methods: Primary human bronchial epithelial cells from four donors were differentiated at air-liquid interface for 30 days and exposed to three cycles of air or CBD- (12.5%) or THC-dominant (20.2%) cannabis smoke generated with or without a cellulose-acetate filter. Barrier function, epithelial denudation, mediator release and epithelial cell protein markers were assessed. Cannabinoids captured from combustion trials of CBD and THC-dominant cannabis were quantified by LC-MS/MS. Results: Repeated exposure to THC or CBD-dominant cannabis strains decreased barrier function, increased epithelial cell denudation, and resulted in greater cell death. Filtration significantly impeded changes in barrier function, epithelial denudation, and cell-death after exposure to both cannabis products. Filtration reduced THC smoke-induced IL-33, Fas, and TRAIL. Soluble CBD and THC concentrations did not differ significantly between filtered and unfiltered combustion. Despite reducing acute epithelial cell injury and mediator release, filtered smoke did not prevent changes in epithelial cell marker expression profiles. Conclusion: Cellulose-acetate filtration attenuated acute cannabis-smoke-induced epithelial injury and selected mediator responses but did not prevent changes in epithelial cell marker expression profiles associated with differentiated cell states. Measured soluble cannabinoid concentrations did not differ significantly between filtered and unfiltered combustion experiments. Cellulose-acetate filters therefore present a promising harm-reduction strategy for cannabis flower combustion, although it should be noted that like tobacco smoke, negative impacts of cannabis combustion are likely to persist even with filtration.

papers.title: B cell tolerance is dysregulated in people with complex regional pain syndrome: A high-dimensional immunophenotyping study
papers.abstract: Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) is a devastating chronic pain disorder that typically arises after distal limb trauma. It has a complex, multi-system pathophysiology that is not well understood, preventing the development of targeted therapies. Observations of self-reactive antibodies in CRPS patients that can elicit pain hypersensitivity in rodents have established an autoimmune contribution to the onset and maintenance of CRPS-like pain, although the mechanisms underlying this remain unclear. To understand the development of pathogenic autoantibody responses in CRPS, this study performed the first high-dimensional characterisation of B cell activity in a cohort of 42 CRPS patients and 42 matched healthy controls. Immunophenotyping of peripheral immune cell populations by mass cytometry identified altered frequencies of class-switched and double-negative memory B cell subsets in CRPS, and increased use of autoimmune-associated IGHV1-69 and IGHV4-34 gene-encoded heavy-chains within the class-switched B cell compartment. Additional proteomic and autoantibody assessments identified differences in serum protein and IgA autoantibody profiles that may lead to altered complement signalling and pro-inflammatory cytokine production in CRPS. Together, these findings represent evidence of dysregulated B cell self-tolerance in CRPS that could facilitate production of pathogenic autoantibodies in people with the condition.

papers.title: A single-cell transcriptomic atlas of T cells across murine lymphoid, mucosal, and gland tissues
papers.abstract: T cells play essential roles in immune surveillance, host defense, and tissue homeostasis, with their cellular composition and transcriptional states varying across tissues. In this study, we constructed an integrated single-cell transcriptional atlas of 124,186 T cells from seven organs of healthy mice. We identified shared T cell states with distinct tissue associated distributions and transcriptional features. Further analyses revealed transcriptional changes associated with thymocyte maturation, diverse innate-like and memory-like T cell populations in bone marrow, and distinct regional distributions of CD8-like T cell states in the intestine. The submandibular gland contained diverse naive, helper-associated, and effector-associated T cell states. pySCENIC analysis further revealed tissue associated variation in inferred transcription factor regulon activity within shared T cell populations. Together, these findings provide a single cell reference for understanding T cell heterogeneity across lymphoid and non-lymphoid tissues under physiological conditions.

papers.title: Keratinocyte IL-17RA signaling promotes neutrophil recruitment and clinical lesions in experimental epidermolysis bullosa
papers.abstract: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita (EBA) is an autoimmune blistering disease (AIBD) characterized by anti-type VII collagen autoantibody-mediated tissue injury. Neutrophils have been identified as essential for dermal-epidermal separation in various in vitro and mouse models of EBA. Although interleukin-17 (IL-17) signaling promotes neutrophilic inflammation, its contribution to EBA and the relevant responding cell types remain poorly defined. We investigated the role and cellular targets of IL-17 receptor A (IL-17RA) signaling using an antibody-transfer model of EBA in mice with global IL-17RA deficiency, combined IL-17A/IL-17F deficiency, IL-17F deficiency, or myeloid cell- or keratinocyte-specific IL-17RA deletion. Complementary in vitro assays assessed IL-17A-induced chemokine expression and neutrophil migration. Global IL-17RA deficiency, combined IL-17A/IL-17F deficiency, and IL-17F deficiency significantly reduced disease severity in vivo. Keratinocyte-specific IL-17RA deletion markedly attenuated EBA, whereas myeloid cell-specific deletion did not confer protection. In vitro, IL-17A increased Cxcl1 mRNA expression in keratinocytes and fibroblasts, and conditioned media from stimulated cells promoted neutrophil migration. These findings identify keratinocytes as key cellular targets of IL-17RA signaling in experimental EBA and support a mechanism linking epithelial cytokine responses to neutrophil recruitment and tissue injury. Our data support investigating the keratinocyte IL-17RA pathway as a potential therapeutic target in EBA and related AIBD.

papers.title: GRABS: a content-addressed antibody-antigen binding-affinity dataset with predicted structures and a leak-free benchmark
papers.abstract: Machine-learning prediction of antibody-antigen binding affinity depends as much on the training data as on the model, yet public affinity measurements are scattered across databases with incompatible formats, mix genuine dissociation constants with censored or predicted values, and concentrate most of their label mass on a few heavily mutated targets. We present GRABS (Geometric Resource for Antibody Binding Studies), a curated, content-addressed, structure-ready dataset that consolidates nine public sources, of which the seven with redistributable licenses yield 4,380 canonical antibody-antigen records} (median-collapsed from 4,761 raw measurements), each with an experimentally measured dissociation constant (Kd), paired heavy and light variable regions (VH, VL), and an antigen sequence, covering 2,015 distinct antigen sequences. Every structure, graph, and feature is addressed by a content key, md5(VH+VL+antigen)[:10], and verified non-circularly: each graph's node features are decoded back to sequence and re-hashed, matching the content key for 4,282/4,282 (100%) structure-backed records. This integrity is load-bearing: an alignment ablation shows that a previously-reported strong cross-target result (R2 {approx} 0.415) was a misalignment-mediated source/batch leak that content-key regeneration dissolves. On the resulting leak-free, antigen-cluster-grouped benchmark, cross-target ranking of variants of a held-out antigen collapses to the noise floor (within-held-out-antigen Spearman {rho} {approx} 0 for every model family: sequence, structure, and folding-confidence), with structure giving no advantage, a rigorously leakage-controlled quantification of the limited reach of current methods. GRABS ships model-ready artifacts (Boltz-2 predicted complexes, per-residue ESM-2 embeddings, geometric graphs, feature vectors) with antigen-stratified splits, and is intended for leakage-free benchmarking and within-target affinity ranking (measure-then-rank), not zero-shot prediction for antigens absent from training.

papers.title: Drastic improvement in MHC class I epitope prediction through training data augmentation, generative adversarial network modeling of selfness, and consideration of homology to class II epitopes.
papers.abstract: Accurate identification of immunogenic neoantigens is critical for personalized cancer vaccines but remains hindered by the high false-positive rates of current predictors. Here, we present DeepOmicsNeo, a modular deep learning framework that harmonizes three biological determinants of immunogenicity. The first module, DeepOmicsNeo-Binding, overcomes data scarcity in non-9mer peptide-Class I Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) binding prediction via a novel augmentation strategy that synthesizes pseudo-binders and non-binders by editing non-anchor residues, outperforming its competitors. The second module, DeepOmicsNeo-Selfness, addresses the paucity of negative training data for immunogenicity prediction by utilizing a Generative Adversarial Network trained on around 60 million human self-peptides. This unsupervised approach quantifies selfness to detect immunogenic peptides and the resulting score correlated with IFN-{gamma} secretion by T-cells. The third module, DeepOmicsNeo-H2, exploits the central-region homology between known HLA Class-I and Class-II restricted epitopes. The integrated model, DeepOmicsNeo-Immunogenicity, outperforms state-of-the-art predictors on the TESLA, HiTIDE, and TiTANIAN benchmark datasets.[2.1] Top20 precision, the most important benchmark for clinical utility in personalized cancer vaccine design, was drastically improved over other predictors. Together, these findings indicate that jointly modeling the three complementary features captures biologically meaningful determinants of immunogenicity, supporting DeepOmicsNeo as a robust computational framework for neoantigen prioritization in personalized cancer immunotherapy.

papers.title: Overcoming subtype-specific immune resistance in small cell lung cancer through RNA-based immunotherapy
papers.abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) comprises neuroendocrine (NE) and non-neuroendocrine (non-NE) subtypes with distinct immune landscapes and responses to therapy. Here, we established murine experimental metastases models to investigate RNA vaccination across SCLC subtypes. These exhibited distinct organotrophic properties and differ in both the magnitude and kinetics of interferon-induced MHC-I upregulation. Vaccination controlled non-NE tumors but provided limited survival benefit against NE tumors established in the lung or liver. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing and chromatin accessibility profiling revealed inflammation-associated programs following vaccination shared between organs. To overcome the limited survival benefit of vaccination in NE SCLC, we combined RNA vaccination with liver-targeted RNA-encoded cytokines. This combination markedly prolonged survival of NE tumor-bearing mice and enhanced inflammatory immune activity within the tumor microenvironment. Together, these findings identify vaccination-associated inflammatory programs of potential clinical relevance and warrant further investigation of cytokine combination therapy as strategy to improve immunotherapy in NE SCLC.

papers.title: Measuring the information budget of cross-target antibody affinity generalization: a robust cross-target wall, and why structure reaches developability but not affinity
papers.abstract: Structure-based machine learning is widely expected to advance antibody engineering, yet it is unclear how far affinity predictions transfer to new targets, and why. We introduce a noise-corrected, censoring-aware estimator of the cross-target transfer ceiling, {rho}max = {surd}(T/(T+I)), which separates a transferable antibody-intrinsic component (T) from a non-transferable target-specific interaction (I). On deterministic synthetic ground truth the estimator recovers the noise-free ceiling to {+/-} 0.0003, whereas the naive sum-of-squares estimator is biased downward by measurement noise. Applying it from synthetic to real systems, the transferable budget is small, and on real neutralization panels it is not an artefact: the target-specific interaction survives noise and censoring correction. It is strongly regime-dependent, with a two-tier structure: predicting a novel antibody from sequence alone (the design setting) reaches a lower ceiling ({rho} {approx} 0.44 on real breadth data) than ranking a characterized one ({rho} {approx} 0.59), even with a strong protein language model. Synthetic oracles also overstate transferability: an oracle scored on real predicted structures carries about half the budget of a matched synthetic lattice (0.45 vs. 0.81), and real neutralization and escape panels sit well below the synthetic ceiling (0.32-0.68). Under leakage-free antigen-cluster splits, cross-target affinity ranking across every method family collapses to this budget, while within a sampled target a structure-based graph network ranks affinity above off-the-shelf FoldX and GearBind (within-complex Spearman 0.55), and structural surface descriptors predict a surface-driven developability property (hydrophobic aggregation) where sequence-dominated properties (humanness, charge-driven self-association) do not benefit. A controlled ablation attributes the residual within-target signal to the antibody alone: dropping the antigen from the structural model leaves it essentially unchanged (interface {Delta} {rho} between -0.01 and +0.02 across four panels), so for this model the paratope-epitope interface adds no ranking signal over the antibody alone. Models climb toward the budget within a target -- via a measure-then-rank operating mode that recovers top binders 6-8 times more efficiently than random once a target has been sampled -- but none crosses it.

papers.title: Switch from inflammatory signaling to excessive extracellular matrix remodeling in fibrotic fibroblasts attenuates monocyte tissue infiltration
papers.abstract: Tissue damage induces infiltration of monocytes that differentiate into macrophages and cooperate with fibroblasts in tissue repair. If repair fails and tissue stress persists, a feedforward loop involving high contractility of activated fibroblasts, extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffening, and TGF-{beta}1 signaling can lead to chronic fibrosis characterized by hypertrophic scarring. In advanced fibrotic tissues areas devoid of immune infiltration have been detected but how the interplay between chemotactic signals versus ECM remodeling impacts monocyte infiltration and spatial positioning in such late-stage fibrotic tissues is unresolved. To address this, we designed a series of 3D co-culture formats incorporating fibrillar collagen I-based ECM, human fibroblasts, and primary human monocytes. RNA-seq, secretome analysis, and confocal microscopy showed that collagen-embedded fibroblasts strongly upregulated inflammatory signaling compared to 2D fibroblast cultures. Incorporation of fibroblasts enhanced collagen fiber network porosity and stimulated monocyte entry into collagen hydrogels and their migration within the collagen network. TGF-{beta}1 activation of collagen-embedded fibroblasts caused a striking switch from inflammatory signaling to an ECM remodeling signature, which was accompanied by local ECM accumulation around fibroblasts and a pronounced increase in collagen fiber network pore size. This did not affect overall fibroblast-stimulated monocyte migration through the ECM, but it prevented monocytes from crossing liquid-hydrogel barriers to penetrate the collagen network. Moreover, it caused excessive ECM remodeling near clusters of fibroblasts, which locally arrested monocyte migration. These findings indicate that excessive fibroblast activation in fibrotic tissues can shift the balance from chemotactic cues toward biomechanical constraints, which limits monocyte infiltration and locally restricts monocyte migration.

papers.title: Cell identity and activation state determine the innate immune response to nanoplastics
papers.abstract: Autoimmune disease is on the rise, and while no direct connection has been made, evidence suggests environmental toxins such as nanoplastics may be contributing to the increased incidence. A key factor in the onset of autoimmunity is inflammation; yet how nanoplastics impact innate immune function is unclear. Here, we exposed primary human neutrophils, macrophages, and endothelial cells to biocorona-coated polystyrene nanoplastics at physiologically relevant concentrations. All cells internalized nanoplastics without viability loss, but functional consequences diverged. Neutrophils increased myeloperoxidase release as nanoplastic concentration increased. Endothelial cells reduced leukocyte-recruiting mediator secretion and had decreased neutrophil adhesion following inflammatory stimulation. M1 macrophages broadly upregulated inflammatory cytokine secretion (including TNF- and IL-6), whereas M0 and M2 macrophages exhibited no significant secretory changes. Collectively, these findings indicate physiologically relevant nanoplastic concentrations do not universally increase inflammation but rather dysregulate innate immune populations in a manner that could contribute to autoimmunity.

papers.title: Continuous generation of short-lived resident effector CD8 T cells sustains alopecia areata
papers.abstract: CD8 T cells mediating chronic tissue inflammation have been thought to depend on stem-like progenitors that self-renew and replenish cytotoxic effector cells or exhausted progeny. Here, we show that stem-independent, short-lived resident effector CD8 T (TRE) cells sustain alopecia areata (AA), a common autoimmune disease that destroys hair follicles. AA-TRE cells exhibit TCR-dependent cytotoxicity, undergo rapid apoptosis in the skin, and lack memory or stem-like properties. Following adoptive transfer, donor TRE cells serve only as an initial trigger, whereas the host-derived CD103CD101 pathogenic pool is rebuilt continuously in skin-draining lymph nodes (sdLNs). Single-cell multiome and CUT&Tag profiling revealed that AA-TRE cells epigenetically silence Tox and upregulate RUNX2 to initiate the TRE differentiation program in sdLNs, while RUNX3 and AP-1s sustain it in the skin. Notably, CD8 T cells from patients with AA share this conserved regulatory network. Altogether, these findings define a distinct CD8 T cell differentiation state, offering new therapeutic implications for autoimmune diseases.

papers.title: Spatial atlas of gut-draining lymph nodes reveals the developmental organization of intestinal tolerance and immunity
papers.abstract: Early life offers a window to establish lasting tolerance to dietary and commensal microbial antigens. How developing gut lymph nodes balance tolerance and immunity remains unclear. Using spatial transcriptomics, we map small intestine- and colon-draining nodes during weaning and adulthood, resolving rare immune and stromal populations and their niches, including Thetis cells (TCs), an antigen-presenting lineage critical for intestinal tolerance. We uncover a peri-weaning subcapsular compartment enriched for TC I but depleted of classical antigen-relaying macrophages, coincident with attenuated follicular responses. Peri-weaning colonic nodes are hubs of T cell activation enriched for peripherally-induced regulatory T (pTreg) cell responses. We resolve distinct classical dendritic cell (cDC) and TC niches, including a pTreg-associated niche shared by TC IV and CCR7 cDC2. We further characterize a distinct population of intestinal tissue TCs, and establish TC migration to draining lymph nodes. Together, our atlas provides a framework for understanding how the timing of intestinal antigen exposure intersects with developing lymph node niches to shape tolerance or immunity.

papers.title: FOLR2 Identifies Functionally Distinct Decidual Macrophage Populations that Coordinate Immune and Tissue Remodelling During Human Labour
papers.abstract: The initiation of human labour remains incompletely understood, although mounting evidence implicates decidual macrophages in this process. Despite this, macrophage heterogeneity remains poorly defined, with current macrophage classification systems, including M1/M2, failing to capture their biological diversity. Here, we investigate whether macrophage differentiation state, defined by expression of the tissue residency marker FOLR2, provides a more informative framework for characterising human decidual macrophages at term. RNA sequencing and flow cytometry identified FOLR2- and FOLR2+ macrophages as transcriptionally and phenotypically distinct populations. FOLR2- macrophages displayed features consistent with recently recruited monocyte-derived cells and were characterised by enrichment of inflammatory and leukocyte recruitment pathways, with greater expression of IL-8 and CCL5 than FOLR2 macrophages. In contrast, FOLR2 macrophages expressed higher levels of MHC class II molecules, CCL2, IL-6, MMP9 and MMP19, and demonstrated the capacity to degrade collagen in fetal membrane explants. Monocyte and macrophage numbers peaked during early labour in the decidua parietalis, accompanied by increased CCL5 expression, whereas FOLR2+ macrophage expression of MMP9 was highest prior to labour. These findings suggest that decidual macrophage heterogeneity is best understood through differentiation state rather than M1/M2 polarisation and point to complementary roles for FOLR2- and FOLR2 macrophages in leukocyte recruitment, tissue remodelling and the local adaptations required for labour initiation and progression.

papers.title: A Dysregulated Peripheral Immune Landscape Favors the Expansion of Epstein-Barr Virus positive Age-Associated B Cells in Multiple Sclerosis
papers.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is a major risk factor for multiple sclerosis (MS), but the underlying mechanisms are not yet known. Here, we use single-cell RNA sequencing coupled with targeted EBV transcript enrichment to characterize host immune and viral transcriptional dynamics following EBV ex vivo infection of PBMCs from people with active MS compared to healthy controls (HC). Early responses to EBV were dominated by differences in monocyte and NK cells, including EBV transcripts in monocytes prior to ex vivo infection. At later time points, expansion of EBV-infected age-associated B-cells (ABCs) and increased expression of T-cell exhaustion- associated markers were elevated in MS. EBV-infected ABCs were deregulated for EBV lytic genes and cellular pathways associated with interferon-alpha responses, antigen processing and Toll-like receptor signaling. Together, these findings define an MS-associated inflammatory immune state and dysfunctional response that favors the formation of pathogenic EBV-infected ABCs.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Refractive Index Patterns Distinguish CD57-Defined Subsets of Human Memory T Cells
papers.abstract: Distinguishing T-cell subsets is important for characterizing immune differentiation, but label-free classification is challenging because closely related subsets have overlapping biophysical properties. We combined holotomography with a three-dimensional convolutional neural network to classify primary human T cells from their refractive index (RI) tomograms. Fluorescence-activated cell sorting defined four reference populations: CD4+, naive CD8+, and CD57- and CD57+ memory CD8+ T cells. The FishNet-inspired classifier achieved 97.04% accuracy in a cell-level held-out test of 270 cells. Dedicated binary classifiers achieved 97.70% accuracy for naive versus CCR7- memory CD8+ cells and 94.44% for CD57- versus CD57+ memory CD8+ cells. Although the memory subsets overlapped in whole-cell descriptors, their volumetric RI patterns supported classification. These findings establish a basis for investigating intrinsic optical phenotypes associated with CD57-defined T-cell differentiation.

papers.title: Biphasic glycocalyx remodelling balances immune cell recruitment and tissue damage during influenza infection
papers.abstract: The endothelial glycocalyx is a glycan-rich barrier lining blood vessels that regulates immune cell recruitment, whose role in viral infection is unknown. Using a murine influenza model, we reveal that the lung endothelial glycocalyx undergoes coordinated biphasic remodelling: early shedding followed by substantial accumulation during peak immune activation. Genetic deletion of heparanase, the enzyme driving early glycocalyx shedding, reduced immune cell lung infiltration and improved host recovery. Conversely, using a new endothelial-specific glycocalyx depletion mouse model, we demonstrate that this glycocalyx accumulation actively limits immune cell recruitment and prevents excessive tissue damage. Together, these findings reveal that coordinated endothelial and immune cell glycocalyx remodelling is an active and previously unrecognised regulator of the balance between antiviral immune cell recruitment and tissue protection.

papers.title: The decidual microenvironment shapes neutrophil subsets that promote extravillous trophoblast invasion in early pregnancy
papers.abstract: Successful establishment of the maternal-fetal interface is a critical process during early pregnancy, ensuring healthy fetal development. A critical phase in establishing the utero-placental blood supply is the invasion of extravillous trophoblasts (EVTs) into the maternal spiral arteries, marking the transformation of the endometrium into the decidua. By separating the EVT invaded decidua (iDec) and EVT non-invaded decidua (niDec), we demonstrate that neutrophils dominate the iDec immune landscape during early human pregnancy. High-dimensional flow cytometry and single-cell transcriptomics revealed that the decidualized microenvironment extends neutrophil survival and shapes discrete tissue-resident subsets, including an activated CD63high phenotype. Imaging mass cytometry uncovered a precise spatial organization, demonstrating preferential cell-cell interactions between these activated neutrophils and invading EVTs. Furthermore, functional in vitro assays demonstrated that the neutrophil secretome, including the core granular protease neutrophil elastase, directly stimulates EVT invasion. Together, these findings identify decidua-associated neutrophils as crucial cellular coordinators of human placental development.

papers.title: Spatially-Organized Adaptive Immune Niches in Granulomas Dictate Local Defense and Correlate with Disease Severity in Tuberculosis Patients
papers.abstract: The cellular composition and spatial organization of immune responses within tuberculosis (TB) granulomas have been increasingly characterized, yet how these spatially organized immune cell populations coordinate local adaptive immunity remains largely unknown. Here, we integrated single-cell multi-omics, spatial transcriptomics, and immune receptor profiling to construct a comprehensive spatial atlas of human TB granulomas. We identified two concentric adaptive immune niches surrounding the central necrotic core. The outer niche comprised granuloma-associated tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) that supported TFH-B cell interactions and exhibited functional germinal center-like features associated with antigen-driven B-cell maturation toward FCRL5 antibody-producing cells. The inner niche contained antigen-experienced and Mtb-reactive effector memory CD8 T cells (TEM), which were recruited from distal lung regions by LGALS9high chemokine-expressing macrophages and activated to undergo local clonal expansion. In lgals9l1 deficient zebrafish, macrophage depletion was accompanied by marked reductions in T- and B-cell enrichment within granulomas and increased bacterial loads, supporting a role for LGALS9high macrophages in coordinating local adaptive immunity against TB infection. Finally, AI-based prediction of spatial gene expression from clinical hematoxylin and eosin-stained specimens revealed that inferred TLS abundance increased with TB disease severity. These findings identify spatially interconnected adaptive immune niches that organize protective immune responses within human TB granulomas, therefore providing a foundation for understanding granuloma adaptive immunity and developing host-directed therapies and vaccines for TB (https://tbomics.smart-nbc.org.cn/).

papers.title: Intestinal goblet cell loss induces microbiota-independent mucosal and systemic IgA dysregulation
papers.abstract: Goblet cells are essential for establishing the intestinal mucus layer and exert diverse immunomodulatory functions. The mucus barrier cooperates with secretory immunoglobulin A (IgA) to regulate host-microbiota interactions and maintain intestinal immune homeostasis. The extent to which goblet cells directly regulate IgA responses remains unclear. Here, we show that depletion of Muc2-expressing intestinal secretory cells in mice caused barrier dysfunction and intestinal inflammation accompanied by profound mucosal and systemic IgA dysregulation, including hyper-IgA, circulating IgA-IgG immune complexes and renal IgA deposition. Selective Paneth cell depletion did not reproduce these IgA abnormalities, and Muc2-deficient mice showed an intermediate phenotype, implicating loss of goblet-cells rather than Paneth cells or of Muc2 loss in this phenotype. Germ-free rederivation markedly attenuated intestinal inflammation but did not prevent mucosal and systemic hyper-IgA or IgA-IgG immune-complex formation, demonstrating that goblet cell loss drives IgA dysregulation independently of live microbial colonisation. Goblet cell loss and IgA deficiency shaped the mucosa-associated microbiota largely independently, as goblet cell depletion promotes expansion of the genus Akkermansia, whereas IgA deficiency reduced Akkermansia but allowed expansion of Mucispirillum and aggravated colonic pathology, indicating that elevated IgA response is partially protective. These findings reveal goblet cells as critical regulators of mucosal and systemic IgA homeostasis beyond mucus production and point to epithelial-immune interactions as potential contributors to IgA-mediated diseases.

papers.title: Label-Free Lymphocyte Subtype and State Classification by Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy
papers.abstract: Accurate immune cell subtype and functional state profiling are essential for studying immune regulation, disease progression, and therapeutic response. Established single-cell analysis techniques rely heavily on either endpoint, destructive measurements or complex labeling that can potentially affect cell functions. Stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy offers quantitative, label-free imaging of cells and tissues by providing contrast based on subcellular concentrations of intrinsic biomolecules at high spatial and temporal resolution. Here, we demonstrate that Vision Transformer based hyperspectral SRS imaging classification can accurately and non-destructively classify various lymphocyte phenotypes, including lymphocyte lineage (T and B cells), T cell subset and differentiation state (CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, effector, memory, and naive for both), and functional states (naive T, activated T, exhausted T) using fluorescent markers for training. By leveraging attention-based spatial-spectral feature learning, the approach captures biomolecular patterns associated with immune cell identity and state while preserving cells for downstream or longitudinal analysis. This provides a potential platform for label-free immune profiling, live-cell analysis, and longitudinal studies of immune cell type and state transitions.

papers.title: Seroprotection and improved polyfunctional immunity conferred by a YF17D-vectored rabies vaccine
papers.abstract: Rabies remains a major public-health challenge, with pre-exposure vaccination strategies constrained by the need for multiple doses and repeated healthcare visits. Here we describe YF-RabG, a live-attenuated rabies vaccine candidate based on the yellow fever 17D (YF17D) vaccine backbone that stably expresses the rabies virus glycoprotein (RabG). YF-RabG exhibited an attenuated phenotype and favourable safety profile compared with parental YF17D across several preclinical models, including neonatal and immunocompromised mice. A single immunization induced robust humoral and cell-mediated immune responses in non-human primates. Rabies virus-neutralizing antibody titres readily exceeded the widely accepted correlate of protection in mice, hamsters and non-human primates by several orders. Accordingly, vaccination conferred protection against lethal rabies challenge in a range of stringent mouse models, maintained seroprotective antibody levels for at least one year, and increased following a boost using a licensed rabies vaccine. Furthermore, the YF17D vector was readily adapted to accommodate glycoproteins from distant lyssaviruses, generating protective vaccine candidates against Mokola, Lagos bat and Lleida bat lyssaviruses. Collectively, these findings identify YF-RabG as a promising single-dose rabies vaccine candidate and highlight the versatility of the YF17D platform for lyssavirus vaccine development.

papers.title: C3-targeting siRNA Combined with Oseltamivir Alleviates Inflammation and Lung Injury in H1N1-Infected Mice
papers.abstract: Influenza A H1N1 infection can trigger severe inflammatory responses that contribute to pulmonary tissue injury and disease progression. Aberrant complement activation is presumed to contribute to these pathological changes. Nevertheless, it remains unclear whether complement C3 serves as a shared upstream regulatory node linking inflammation and hemolytic injury. In this study, we established an H1N1-infected mouse model to dynamically monitor changes in inflammation, hemolysis and complement-related parameters throughout infection. We evaluated the C3-silencing efficacy of RG002, a liver-targeted siRNA against complement C3, as well as the therapeutic efficacy of RG002 combined with oseltamivir against H1N1 infection. Our results showed that H1N1 infection induced prominent inflammatory responses and alterations in peripheral blood cell parameters, accompanied by pulmonary histopathological injury in mice. Hepatic C3 expression and complement activity were simultaneously and markedly elevated. RG002 suppressed C3 expression in a dose-and time-dependent manner and reduced complement-mediated erythrocyte lysis in serum. In vivo therapeutic experiments demonstrated that on the basis of viral replication suppression achieved by oseltamivir, combination treatment with RG002 inhibited excessive complement activation. This combined regimen reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, attenuated pulmonary histopathological injury, and improved selected peripheral blood cell parameters. Notably the low-dose RG002 combination group exhibited superior performance across multiple evaluation indices, suggesting that the degree of C3 suppression is preferable to influence therapeutic effucaty. Collectively, our findings implicate complement C3 in the inflammatory pathology associated with H1N1 infection and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of C3-targeting siRNA as an adjunct to antiviral treatment. This study provides experimental evidence supporting the combination of antiviral therapy and controlled complement modulation as a potential host-directed therapeutic strategy for severe influenza.

papers.title: From Adalimumab to orally administered secretory IgA: preclinical characterization of ABC-301
papers.abstract: Reformatting therapeutic immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibodies into secretory immunoglobulin A (sIgA) may provide an alternative architecture for mucosal drug delivery. We characterized ABC-301, a recombinant human sIgA1 incorporating the antigen-binding regions of Adalimumab, and evaluated its human tumor necrosis factor alpha (TNF) neutralization, oral activity in experimental colitis, tissue biodistribution, and susceptibility to patient-derived anti-Adalimumab antibodies. ABC-301 retained human TNF binding and functional neutralization in vitro. Its whole-molecule molar neutralization IC50 was approximately 3.3-fold lower than that of Adalimumab, a difference of approximately 1.6-fold after normalization to theoretical binding-site number. In dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis, oral ABC-301 attenuated colon shortening and reduced colonic inflammatory myeloid populations and tissue inflammatory biomarkers relative to untreated DSS controls. Following oral administration, iodine-125-associated radioactivity was predominantly detected in gastrointestinal compartments. In seven patient-derived anti-Adalimumab antibody preparations, ABC-301 showed reduced functional susceptibility to inhibition compared with Adalimumab. These findings provide a preclinical proof of concept for IgG-to-sIgA reformatting.

papers.title: In vitro and in vivo validation of recombinant Syrian hamster interferon-α
papers.abstract: The Syrian hamster (Mesocricetus auratus) is an important model for the study of viral pathogenesis and the development of antiviral drugs and vaccines, yet species-specific reagents remain scarce. Here, we validate the potent and specific activity of recombinantly expressed Syrian hamster maIFN-12-like protein (maIFN) in vitro and in vivo. MaIFN expressed in E. coli induced MX2 and ISG15 expression in both BHK21 hamster kidney cells as well as in primary hamster fibroblasts in a dose-dependent manner and EC50 values in low pg/mL range. Activation was strictly STAT2-dependent and more potent, by at least one order of magnitude, than that achieved by heterologous human or mouse IFN. ISG induction translated into a strong antiviral activity against YF17D virus replication in BHK21 cells as well as ISRE-dependent reporter expression in a newly established hamster reporter cell line. When tested in wild-type but not in STAT2-deficient hamsters, maIFN showed a physiologic, vigorous yet rapidly contracting systemic ISG response. Together these findings establish maIFN as a functional antiviral cytokine and valuable reagent for preclinical infectious disease research using Syrian hamsters.

papers.title: Prim-O-glucosylcimifugin suppresses M2 macrophage polarization via the JAK2-STAT6-PPARγ pathway to alleviate allergic asthma
papers.abstract: Background: Allergic asthma (AA) is a chronic respiratory disease closely linked to immune-inflammatory responses driven by M2 macrophage polarization. PrimO-glucosylcimifugin (POG), a natural bioactive compound from Saposhnikovia divaricata (SD), alleviates inflammation in acute lung injury mice, but whether it mitigates AA by modulating M2 macrophage polarization remains unclear. Objective: This study investigated POGs effects on AA and its mechanisms in regulating M2 macrophage polarization. Methods: LC-MS profiled the SD/Prunus mume (PM) combination, and network pharmacology predicted its main active components and key anti-AA mechanisms. Ovalbumin (OVA) plus IL-4 established AA models in mice and RAW264.7 cells. Lung protection was assessed by histopathology, lung indices, and type II immune inflammatory cytokine markers. Flow Cytometry, RT-qPCR, immunofluorescence, and Western blot examined key genes/proteins in the JAK2-STAT6-PPAR{gamma} axis. Results: LC-MS-based network pharmacology identified POG as the key SD/PM active ingredient alleviating AA. Pharmacodynamic evaluation showed POG effectively alleviated OVA-induced airway inflammation and pulmonary histopathological damage in AA mice. Mechanistically, POG inhibited M2 macrophage polarization by downregulating key JAK2-STAT6-PPAR{gamma} axis factors. Conclusion: POG ameliorates AA by reducing type II immune factor release through JAK2-STAT6-PPAR{gamma}-mediated inhibition of M2 macrophage polarization. This study clarifies POGs anti-AA mechanism and supports its clinical development.

papers.title: Acute hypertension causes focal coronary artery perivascular cGAS-, IRF3, and IFNAR-dependent type I interferon responses
papers.abstract: Hypertension exposes coronary arteries to dynamic mechanical forces that alter the structural integrity and lead to pathologic changes such as aneurysm, dissection, or atherogenesis. Although the effects of chronic hypertension have been extensively studied, the early molecular responses to increased luminal pressure remain poorly understood. Here, we find that acute hypertension in murine coronary arteries induced by transverse aortic constriction (TAC) causes focal perivascular type I interferon (IFN) responses in the vessel wall in contrast to comparatively homogeneous perivascular fibrosis. Spatial transcriptomics and RNAscope independently demonstrate spatially clustered expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in the walls of pressurized left and right coronary arteries in the first week after TAC. Genetic disruption of cGAS or IRF3 each markedly attenuated the perivascular ISG response, indicating the response is a consequence of DNA sensing. Pharmacologic disruption of type I IFN signaling using an anti-IFNAR antibody abolished pressure-induced induction of focal ISG expression suggesting the pathway can be inhibited therapeutically. Since focal type I IFN signaling in the infarct borderzone of the left ventricle increased risk of dilation and rupture, we propose that focal perivascular type I IFN signaling in the vessel wall may serve as a nidus for analogous pathologies like aneurysm, dissection, or atherogenesis and represent a potential target for therapy.

papers.title: SIRT3 preserves mitochondrial DNA integrity to restrain cGAS-STING signaling and autoimmune inflammation
papers.abstract: Mitochondria play critical roles beyond energy production, including regulation of innate immunity through release of damage-associated molecular patterns such as mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA). Sirtuin 3 (SIRT3), a mitochondrial deacetylase, modulates mitochondrial function, reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and inflammation. Here, we investigate the role of SIRT3 in controlling Type I interferon (IFN) responses in macrophages. We show that Sirt3 depletion in mouse macrophages increases basal mtDNA release into the cytosol, activating the cGAS-STING pathway and enhancing the expression of IFN-{beta} and downstream interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs). Accordingly, Sirt3-deficient cells exhibit markedly increased resistance to vesicular stomatitis virus infection. Secreted IFN-{beta} also acts in a paracrine manner, priming neighboring cells and reinforcing antiviral defenses. Using mtDNA-deficient ({rho}0) cells, we demonstrate that intact mtDNA is essential for this amplified interferon response, as mtDNA depletion abolishes IFN-{beta} induction following Sirt3 knockdown. Mechanistically, increased mitochondrial ROS (mtROS) in SIRT3-deficient cells promotes mtDNA leakage and cGAS-STING activation, effects that are attenuated by the mitochondrial superoxide scavenger MitoTEMPO. In vivo, SIRT3 protects against chlorhexidine gluconate-induced peritoneal fibrosis by restraining macrophage infiltration, ISGs expression and fibrotic remodeling, underscoring its role in modulating STING-dependent inflammation and tissue damage. Finally, reanalysis of transcriptomic datasets from patients with lupus nephritis and rheumatoid arthritis reveals reduced SIRT3 expression, suggesting that SIRT3 downregulation is also associated with human inflammatory diseases. Collectively, our findings identify SIRT3 as an important regulator of mitochondrial integrity and oxidative stress that modulates innate immune and antiviral responses.

papers.title: Macaque Vγ4+ γδ T cells exhibit distinct IFN-γ and IL-22 effector profiles that are dysregulated during chronic SIV infection and diarrheal disease
papers.abstract: V{gamma}4+ {gamma}{delta} T cells contribute to colonic homeostasis in humans, but their biology in nonhuman primates remains poorly defined. Here, we characterized V{gamma}4+ {gamma}{delta} T cells in blood and intestinal tissues of healthy, diarrhea-inflicted, and SIV-infected rhesus macaques. TRG/TRD repertoire sequencing across colon, mesenteric lymph node, blood, and spleen revealed compartment-specific clonal architecture and colonic enrichment of TRGV3. Flow cytometric profiling revealed circulating and colonic V{gamma}4+ T cells were predominantly V{delta}1+, exhibited an effector memory phenotype, and displayed T-bet-dominant transcriptional profiles. High-dimensional clustering confirmed V{gamma}4+V{delta}1+ T cells as a distinct terminally differentiated lineage. Functionally, stimulated V{gamma}4+ T cells exhibited robust Th1/Th17 cytokine production, supporting dual inflammatory and barrier-protective roles. Campylobacter-associated diarrhea was characterized by mucosal expansion of central memory V{gamma}4+ T cells and altered cytokine responses. In contrast, ART-suppressed chronic SIV infection was associated with colonic enrichment of naive-like V{gamma}4+ T cells and increased ROR{gamma}t expression, alongside profound systemic loss of cytokine production but relative preservation of mucosal Th17-type responses. Both conditions exhibited a convergent loss of systemic Type 1 effector V{gamma}4+ T-cell responses, pointing to a shared functional alteration during chronic intestinal inflammation. Overall, these findings reveal disease-specific remodeling of V{gamma}4+ T cells during chronic intestinal inflammation and gut barrier disruption in chronic enterocolitis and SIV infection.
